battle.name: 青海之戰
battle.brief: 儀鳳三年（678）春，吐蕃犯青海道，唐以薛仁貴為邽地道行軍大總管，率眾十萬至青海湖東南河口，弩陣拒騎、騎兵反擊而大破之，拔其堡寨、獲牛羊無算，吐蕃乃遣使請和。卡面兵器為埃及月牙劍，屬前1500年上下的單刃彎刀，當時早已絕跡；本役唐軍用陌刀、長槊、唐弩，吐蕃用藏式長刀、長矛與札甲。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 此役交戰雙方是唐與吐蕃。唐朝方面由關隴、河西的邊軍擔當骨幹，大軍自涼州出，經鄯州、河州而進至青海湖東南的河口；出征主力是薛仁貴所領的精騎，關中、中原新募的團練兵與歸附的吐谷渻餘部編在後續梯隊。糧秣靠涼州、河州、鄯州一線的軍倉與屯田，器械、輜重、工匠隨營轉運；軍令由行軍大總管與監軍太監共同副署，兵部在長安調度，而節度使制度尚未建立，故全軍只聽大總管與其副手。吐蕃方面是高原政權，贊普論悉諾羅自領大軍，兵以吐蕃本部的騎隊為骨幹，輔以谷地部眾、被俘的漢地民戶與隨軍冶鐵工匠，駐營逐水草而徙，帳幕、馬群、牛羊隨軍移動，攻城器械薄弱。戰場在青海湖東南、黃河上游的河口一帶，正當唐朝通往西域的青海道東段；雙方爭的不是城池，而是青海道本身：唐要保住西域通道並重立吐谷渻作前哨，吐蕃要掐斷這條路，並獨享青海的牧場與鹽池。
countriesEn: The two parties in this campaign were the Tang dynasty and the Tibetan Empire. On the Tang side the backbone consisted of the frontier armies of Guanzhong and Hexi: the expedition marched out of Liangzhou, passed through Shanzhou and Hezhou, and advanced to Hekou on the southeastern shore of Qinghai Lake. The striking force was the picked cavalry commanded by Xue Rengui, while troops mustered in Guanzhong and in the Central Plain and the remnants of the Tuyuhun who had submitted were formed up as the follow-up echelons. Grain came from the depot stores and the garrison farms strung along Liangzhou, Hezhou and Shanzhou, and weapons, baggage and craftsmen travelled with the column. Orders were countersigned jointly by the Army Grand Commander and the imperial eunuch overseer, the Ministry of War handled dispatch from Chang'an, and since the regional military governorship had not yet been created the entire army answered to the Grand Commander and his deputies alone. Opposite them was a plateau state: the tsipon Lunxi Luoluo led the host in person, the core of which was the cavalry of the Tibetan heartland, supported by valley peoples, Han Chinese villagers carried off into captivity, and the smiths who accompanied the army. The camps moved as the pastures moved; tents, herds of horses, cattle and sheep all travelled with the column, and siege equipment was scarce. The battlefield lay around Hekou on the southeastern shore of Qinghai Lake, on the upper Yellow River, precisely on the eastern stretch of the Qinghai Road that linked the Tang with the western regions. What the two sides fought over was no walled city but the road itself: the Tang needed to keep the corridor toward the west open and to re-establish Tuyuhun as a forward bastion, while the Tibetans wanted to cut that road and to enjoy exclusive control of the pastures and salt lakes of Qinghai.
people: 唐方主帥是薛仁貴，本名薛禮，字仁貴，絳州龍門人，出身行伍，父祖皆軍籍；他在太宗帳下效力，永徽年間隨軍破突厥於磧口，又在高句麗之役中以行軍總管身份參與攻滅之役，靠白袍先登與輕騎追斬屢立功，到儀鳳三年已是唐廷倚重的邊將，遂受命為邽地道行軍大總管，率眾十萬出討。吐蕃方面，主帥是贊普論悉諾羅——漢譯名在史籍中不一，亦有作論悉羅者；他以數十萬眾的規模壓向青海，具體的臨陣統帥，古籍或稱大論一類的近臣，或稱其別部，記載互有出入。可以考定的有兩點：這場戰爭由贊普本人決意發動；其名號在不同史籍寫法有別，不必過度考究。唐廷方面則是高宗下詔出兵、兵部在長安調度諸軍、監軍太監隨軍牽制，總管之下設副總管數人與行軍司馬，兵將名姓在《舊唐書》《新唐書》與《資治通鑑》之間多有出入，後人難以一一對應。此外，唐初即議重立的吐谷渻客戶國，其舊部首領與部眾也是這條戰線上的隱性角色：吐蕃若據青海，即斷唐之臂；若唐扶起吐谷渻，即在吐蕃身側插刀。
peopleEn: The Tang commander was Xue Rengui, born Xue Li and known by the courtesy name Rengui, a native of Longmen in Jiangzhou, born into the ranks and descended from military households on both sides of the family. He had served in the camp of Emperor Taizong, campaigned with the army that broke the Turks at Qikou in the Yonghui era, and later took part as an Army Commander in the campaign that destroyed Goguryeo, winning renown for leading in white robes and for light cavalry pursuits; by the third year of Yifeng he was a frontier general on whom the court relied, and he was accordingly appointed Grand Commander of the Army for the Guizhou Circuit and marched out with a hundred thousand men. On the Tibetan side the commander in chief was the tsipon Lunxi Luoluo, whose name appears in Chinese sources in several renderings, one of them simply Lunxi Luoluo; he pressed towards Qinghai with a host counted in tens of thousands, and for the actual command on the field the records variously name high ministers of the title Dalun or the commanders of his other divisions, and they do not agree. Two things can be settled: the war was launched on the tsipon's own decision, and his name is written differently in different chronicles, so there is no need to press the point. On the Tang side the emperor Gaozong issued the orders, the Ministry of War coordinated the armies from Chang'an, and an eunuch overseer travelled with the column to keep the general in check; under the Grand Commander sat several deputy commanders and a military judge, and the names of officers and men differ from one of the Old Book of Tang, the New Book of Tang and the Comprehensive Mirror to the other, so they cannot be matched one by one. Besides all this, the Tuyuhun client state that the Tang had proposed to restore in the early years of the reign, with its own leaders and people, played a hidden role on this front: if the Tibetans held Qinghai they cut the Tang's arm, while if the Tang raised the Tuyuhun up again they planted a knife at the Tibetans' flank.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是埃及月牙劍（Khopesh），約成形於前1500年前後的埃及中王朝，單刃、外彎，刃口走內凹的弧，砍進人身不必像直劍那樣拔出；它的形制承自埃及早王朝的斧形冷兵器，銅或青銅質，配木柄、骨柄與皮纏握把，是尼羅河文明最早定型的近戰兵器之一。但在本役裡它並不、也不可能出現：678年的埃及在倭馬亞王朝治下，這種劍式在埃及早已絕跡，殘存的實物要到19世紀才在開羅的古董市場與歐洲的藏品中重新浮現，20世紀更成了旅遊紀念品與武術道具。換言之，埃及月牙劍在本卡的作用是時間標尺——它屬於文字記載之前數千年的工藝傳統，與本役年代相隔約二千二百年。本役真正登上青海草場的兵器是：唐軍的陌刀、直刃環首刀、長槊、唐弩與蹶張弩、弓箭、圓盾與拒馬、明光鎧甲，以及涼州、河州牧場的軍馬；吐蕃軍則是唐人記作沙魚的長劍（以犀皮為鞘）、矛盾器械、鑲金銀的牛皮與獸皮鎧甲、彎弓與長矛。兩邊都備投石、撞車、巢車與飛雲梯一類攻城器，也都靠牛羊馱載輜重；西域方面，同期的波斯與大食正流行薩珊式的彎刀，那才是月牙劍形制的同源遠親，卻也不是卡面上這一件。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh, a shape that took form around 1500 BCE in the Middle Kingdom: single edged and outward curved, with a concave cutting edge, so that once it had been driven into a body it did not have to be pulled back out the way a straight sword must be. Its form descends from the axe shaped blades of Egypt's Early Dynastic period; it was made of copper or bronze, fitted with a wooden or bone haft and a leather bound grip, and it is one of the earliest close combat weapons ever standardised in the civilisation of the Nile. Yet in this campaign it neither appeared nor could have appeared. Egypt in 678 stood under the Umayyad caliphate, and the form had long been extinct in the country itself; the surviving examples only re-emerged in the antique markets of Cairo and in European collections in the nineteenth century, and in the twentieth they became souvenirs and sporting props. In other words the khopesh on this card works as a time scale: it belongs to a craft tradition thousands of years before written record, roughly two thousand two hundred years separated from the fighting described here. The blades that actually reached the pastures of Qinghai were these. The Tang carried the miao dao, the straight edged ring pommel saber, the long spear, the Tang crossbow and the strong arm crossbow, bows and arrows, round shields and cheval de frise, and bright armour of the ming guang type, together with the garrison horses of the Liangzhou and Hezhou pastures. The Tibetans carried the long sword that Chinese sources call the shayu, sheathed in rhinoceros hide, their lance and javelin contrivances, hide and leather armour inlaid with gold and silver, composite bows and long spears. Both sides brought up stone throwers, battering rams, scaling towers and cloud ladders of their sort, and both loaded their baggage on cattle and sheep. In the west the Persians and the Arabs of this same period were carrying Sasanian curved blades; those, not this, are the close relatives of the khopesh line.
tactics: 唐軍的部署圍繞據險、耗騎、反擊、清野四步。薛仁貴自涼州出師後不與吐蕃騎隊爭先馳援，而是把營紮在青海湖東南、河道兩側的高地與土梁之間，先環挖壕塹、擺列拒馬與鹿角，再把弩手分層排在塹後，弓手壓頂，騎兵在後待機。吐蕃大軍列陣而來，密集騎隊在狹窄草地上難以展開，只能一波一波衝擊唐軍的弩陣與槍陣；唐軍不與之纏鬥，只以弩矢與箭雨消耗其前鋒，待其人馬疲憊、隊形散亂，才開門放出精騎反擊，追擊數十里。這一戰術的要害不在個人武藝，而在弓弩的密度與地形的限制：唐軍用工事折掉吐蕃的兵力優勢，再用騎兵在開闊處收穫成果。吐蕃的應對則是典型的遊擊保存：避開唐軍鋒芒、掠奪牛羊與糧秣、封鎖青海道、切斷漢地運糧的通道、必要時退入高原草原重整，一旦戰局不利便連夜拔營，令唐軍追之不上。唐軍的弱點也正暴露在此：糧秣要自涼州、河州千里輸送，冬季草枯雪深，牛馬易斃，戰事拖長即成死局；吐蕃營中無城壘、也無攻城器械，同樣難以攻取唐軍的城鎮。
tacticsEn: The Tang deployment followed four steps: take the ground, wear down the horsemen, counterattack, clear the ground. After leaving Liangzhou, Xue Rengui did not race to meet the Tibetan cavalry but planted his camp among the heights and loess ridges on both sides of the river on the southeastern shore of Qinghai Lake. He had a ring trench dug, set cheval de frise and spiked abatis along it, ranged the crossbowmen in tiers behind the trench, kept archers on the heights and the cavalry waiting in the rear. The Tibetan host came up in line, and a dense mass of horsemen could not deploy on narrow grassland; it could only surge against the Tang trench in successive waves. The Tang declined to be drawn into a melee, spending the enemy's leading elements with bolts and arrow-fall, and only when the horses were spent and the formation had come apart did the camp gates open and the picked cavalry strike out, pursuing for tens of li. The crux of this was not individual swordsmanship but the density of the crossbows and the restrictions of the ground: the Tang used field works to cancel the Tibetans' advantage in numbers, then used cavalry to harvest the result on open ground. The Tibetan response was typical of raiding and preservation: keep away from the Tang edge, take cattle, sheep and grain, blockade the Qinghai Road, cut the Chinese supply line, and when necessary fall back into the high grasslands to refit; when the battle turned they broke camp by night so that the Tang could not overtake them. The Tang weakness showed in the same place. Grain had to be dragged a thousand li from Liangzhou and Hezhou, in winter the grass died and the snow deepened, oxen and horses died easily, and a campaign that dragged on became a dead end; the Tibetan camp had no walls and no siege engines either, so they too found it hard to take Tang fortified towns.
data: 可核對的數字有限，只能列出史籍明載與合理推算的部分。唐軍出動兵力的舊史記載是「率眾十萬」，以騎兵為多數，關中、中原募兵與歸附部眾在後續梯隊；吐蕃一方的總數，舊史或稱四十萬、或稱二十餘萬，兩說相差近一倍，較穩妥的判斷是投入的騎隊以數萬計。戰果方面，記載多稱「斬首數千級」，俘獲人數與繳獲牛羊則常以無算、數十萬形容；唐軍還拔取吐蕃在青海的堡寨數十座，奪其帳幕、馬匹與牛羊，這批畜牧同時是補給與戰利。行程上，自涼州至青海湖東南河口，陸路逾一千公里，中間要穿過祁連山南麓的隘口；時間上，自儀鳳三年三月出師到秋初罷兵，前後約數月。武器形制方面，埃及月牙劍的現存實物多在半米上下，屬短兵器，與本役的陌刀、長槊這類長兵器不同量級。三點提醒：一是唐蕃雙方在青海的記載本身殘缺，數字多有誇飾；二是斬獲多為方帥上報的通報數，不等於逐戰實錄；三是關於兵力的記載多出自獲勝一方的史官，敗方數字常被壓低。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are few, and only those recorded in the histories together with reasonable inference can be set down. The old records give the Tang force as a hundred thousand men, cavalry for the most part, with recruits from Guanzhong and the Central Plain and the submitted peoples in the follow-up echelons. For the Tibetans the old records say either four hundred thousand or a little over two hundred thousand, a difference of nearly double; the safer judgement is that the cavalry actually committed was numbered in tens of thousands. On results the accounts commonly speak of several thousand severed heads, while prisoners and captured cattle and sheep are described as countless or as tens of thousands; the Tang also took a number of Tibetan forts in Qinghai, some dozens of them, with their tents, horses and herds, and that livestock was at once supply and prize. As to distance, the land route from Liangzhou to Hekou on the southeastern shore of Qinghai Lake runs past a thousand kilometres, and it has to cross the passes of the southern foot of the Qilian range. As to time, from the departure in the third month of the third year of Yifeng to the standing down of the army in early autumn, some months passed. As to the weapon forms, the surviving Egyptian khopesh specimens run to about half a metre and belong to the short blade class, a different order of magnitude from the miao dao and long spears of this campaign. Three cautions. First, the Tibetan and Tang records for Qinghai are themselves fragmentary, and the numbers are often inflated. Second, the tallies of kills and captures are mostly the dispatch figures reported by the winning commander and are not a record of each engagement. Third, the troop figures we have come largely from the chroniclers of the victor, and the defeated side's numbers are habitually understated.
cause: 打起來有遠因也有近因。遠因是咸亨元年（670）秋那場青海道的大敗：唐軍在青海湖西南的大非川潰散，士卒死傷過半，統軍的宗室將領被俘，青海道自此中斷，通西域的支線斷了三年多，涼州與河州直接暴露在吐蕃騎兵面前。此後數年，唐廷一直在謀劃東出：重立吐谷渻客戶國、在青海一線設堡屯田、派大將率精兵收復失地；吐蕃也清楚唐一旦重開青海道，自己的東進與西域經商都會受制，於是搶先動手。近因是儀鳳三年（678）春，吐蕃大軍再越邊境，深入青海一帶的邊城劫掠，唐不得不出兵應戰。雙方的爭點其實是三樣東西：青海道上行軍的安全、湖邊的牧場與鹽池、以及通往西域的商路與使節通道。和親與贈禮曾經試過——唐初以文成公主嫁吐蕃，高宗永徽年間又遣裴行儉送獅子與大批器物給贊普，兩國一度以禮物換和平——但此後數年的記錄裡，和議始終沒有能壓住邊境上的反覆衝突。
causeEn: The war had both remote and immediate causes. The remote cause was the great defeat on the Qinghai Road in the autumn of the first year of Xianheng, 670: the Tang army broke up at Dafeichuan in the southwest of Qinghai Lake, more than half of the soldiers were killed or wounded, the imperial clansman who commanded was taken prisoner, and the Qinghai Road was cut from that day, the branch line to the western regions broken for more than three years, with Liangzhou and Hezhou left directly exposed to Tibetan horsemen. In the years that followed the Tang court never stopped planning an eastward thrust: to restore the Tuyuhun client state, to build forts and garrison farms along the Qinghai line, to send a great general with picked troops to recover the lost ground. The Tibetans knew just as well that once the Tang reopened the Qinghai Road their own advance east and their western trade would be constrained, so they struck first. The immediate cause was the spring of the third year of Yifeng, 678, when the Tibetan host crossed the frontier again, struck deep into the border towns around Qinghai and carried off stores, and the Tang had no choice but to answer. What the two sides actually disputed was three things: the safety of marching on the Qinghai Road, the pastures and salt lakes along the lake shore, and the trade routes and channels of envoys leading to the west. Marriage alliance and gifts had been tried before. The Tang had given the Wencheng princess to a Tibetan ruler in the early years of the reign, and in the Yonghui era of Gaozong they sent Pei Xingjian with a lion and a great quantity of goods to the tsipon, and for a time the two countries exchanged peace for presents. But in the records of the years that followed no negotiated peace ever suppressed the repeated collisions on the frontier.
impact: 影響分三層。第一層是戰線本身：678年這場勝利讓唐朝短時間拿回青海湖東南的幾處據點，青海道東段一度重開，涼州、河州一線的邊防壓力稍減；吐蕃請和之後兩國有數年相安，直到開元初年吐蕃再攻涼州、臨洮一帶，唐廷終於放棄讓吐谷渻復國的打算，青海道長期落在吐蕃手中。第二層是唐朝自身的體制：此役暴露了關隴兵制與糧秣制度的短板，關中宿衛的戰力退化、邊軍靠募兵與和市維持，都促使朝廷在河西與隴右試驗新的軍鎮與屯田體制，日後的河西節度使與長城沿線的軍鎮化，其源頭都能追到青海戰線的失與得。第三層是兵器與工藝的意義：這一役是中原冷兵器與高原冷兵器的一次直接對照——唐軍以陌刀、長槊、唐弩和明光甲構成的正面戰鬥力，遇上以彎弓、長矛、札甲和遊擊機動為主的部落軍隊；同一時期在西方，阿拉伯帝國在薩珊崩潰的廢墟上崛起，彎刀與騎射的傳統在另一方天地間快速成熟。卡面選用的埃及月牙劍正好標示出這條時間軸的另一端：同一種砍下去不用拔的單刃彎刀，在尼羅河流域是前1500年的古物，在7世紀的歐亞則已是別處的活傳統。
impactEn: The consequences work on three levels. The first is the front itself. This victory of 678 allowed the Tang for a short time to retake several strongholds on the southeastern shore of Qinghai Lake; the eastern stretch of the Qinghai Road was reopened, and the pressure on the Liangzhou and Hezhou line eased a little. After the Tibetan request for peace the two countries lived in quiet for a number of years, until in the early Kaiyuan years the Tibetans attacked Liangzhou and Lintao once more, the court finally abandoned the plan of restoring the Tuyuhun, and the Qinghai Road remained in Tibetan hands for a long stretch. The second level is Tang institutions themselves. This campaign laid bare the weaknesses of the military system and of the supply arrangements in Guanzhong and Longyou: the fighting quality of the palace guards in the capital had decayed, and the frontier troops were sustained by recruitment and by the border markets. All of it urged the court to try new military districts and garrison farms in Hexi and Longyou, and the later military governorship of Hexi and the fortified-line districts along the Great Wall can all be traced back to what was won and lost on the Qinghai front. The third level is the matter of weapons and craft. This was a direct confrontation between cold weapons of the Chinese plain and cold weapons of the high plateau: the frontal strength built from miao dao, long spears, Tang crossbows and bright armour met a tribal host whose strength lay in composite bows, long spears, lamellar armour and mobile raiding. At the same time in the west the Arab empire was rising on the ruins of the collapsed Sasanian state, and the traditions of the curved blade and mounted archery were maturing fast in another part of the world. The Egyptian khopesh chosen for the card marks the far end of that same time line: the single edged curved blade that does not need to be pulled out after the blow was a relic of some 1500 BCE on the Nile, but in the seventh century Eurasia it was a living tradition elsewhere.
result: 結果可以分戰術與戰略兩層講。戰術上唐軍在河口打贏了：弩陣耗掉吐蕃騎隊的鋒頭，騎兵反擊得其銳氣，唐軍乘勝拔堡、追奔、繳獲牛羊，吐蕃請和。這一仗是唐蕃戰爭中唐軍少數乾淨的野戰勝利之一。戰略上只能算打平：唐軍沒有足夠的後續兵力與糧秣把優勢轉成佔領，青海湖一線仍在吐蕃控制之下，鹽池與牧場也未到手；和議維持了數年，很快被新的進攻取代。三個要說清的保留：一是這場戰役的史源主要靠《舊唐書》《新唐書》《資治通鑑》，三者年代與編纂先後不一，彼此對人數、斬獲與日期多有出入；二是論悉諾羅的名號在文獻中有譯名與轉寫的混雜，不必過度考究；三是後人常把678年河口之役與670年大非川之敗混為一件事，前者是唐軍得手，後者是唐軍崩敗，本役只屬前者。總體而言，這是一場把唐蕃長期消耗戰推入新階段的戰役：唐朝以一次戰術勝利換來數年喘息，吐蕃以讓步換取時間，兩邊都清楚真正的勝負還在後面的青海道上。
resultEn: The outcome can be read on two levels, tactical and strategic. Tactically the Tang won at Hekou: the crossbow line spent the leading edge of the Tibetan cavalry, the counterstroke by the mounted troops took the fight out of them, and the Tang pressed on to take the forts, to pursue and to carry off cattle and sheep, and the Tibetans asked for peace. This was one of the few clean field victories the Tang won in the long Tang Tibetan war. Strategically it amounts to a draw. The Tang had neither the follow-up troops nor the grain to turn the advantage into occupation; the line of Qinghai Lake remained under Tibetan control, and neither the salt lakes nor the pastures came into Tang hands. The negotiated peace lasted a number of years and was soon overtaken by fresh attacks. Three reservations should be stated. First, the sources for this campaign are chiefly the Old Book of Tang, the New Book of Tang and the Comprehensive Mirror; the three differ in date and in the order of their compilation, and they disagree about numbers, captures and chronology. Second, the name Lunxi Luoluo is tangled in the documents through translation and transliteration, and there is no need to press the point. Third, later writers often run together the battle at Hekou in 678 and the defeat at Dafeichuan in 670; the first was a Tang success, the second a Tang collapse, and only the former belongs to this campaign. On the whole this was a battle that pushed the long attrition between Tang and Tibet into a new phase: the Tang bought a few years of breath with one tactical victory, the Tibetans bought time with a concession, and both understood that the real decision still lay further along the Qinghai Road.
